expected_prisoner.name: Jo An Yellow Bird
expected_prisoner.description: Jo An Yellow Bird was an American Indian Movement activist married to Nebraska AIM coordinator Bob Yellow Bird. In 1976, police arrested the couple after Bob called to report that a white man had choked and maced him. Officers charged both with malicious destruction of property. A contemporary account reported that an officer kicked Jo An Yellow Bird in the stomach during the arrest, causing her to lose her pregnancy. The report does not give her custody dates or the final disposition.

expected_cases.sentence: Arrest documented, but exact custody dates and final disposition have not been located.

case.charges: Disorderly conduct following an earlier 1976 confrontation at her home; originally also accused of resisting and abusing an officer.
case.plead: Pleaded to the lesser offense of disorderly conduct
case.sentence: Served two days for disorderly conduct in 1976, before the separate September 15 arrest. Exact admission and release dates are not established. W. Dale Mason describes the plea and actual two days served in his account of AIM organizing in Nebraska. Source: https://www.oocities.org/lakotastudentalliance/lsa2_onlykicksolong.html

case.charges: Disorderly conduct following the September 15, 1976 confrontation outside the Sheridan Hotel and Lounge in Gordon, Nebraska.
case.sentence: Arrested and taken in handcuffs to the county jail in Rushville on September 15, 1976. After several hours in jail she was taken to Gordon Memorial Hospital and then referred to the Pine Ridge hospital. Mason reports later hospital discharge on condition she not be returned to jail, but gives no exact discharge date. Hospitalization is not recorded here as a measured prison sentence. This is separate from the earlier two-day disorderly-conduct term. Source: https://www.oocities.org/lakotastudentalliance/lsa2_onlykicksolong.html
